book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 11

clue.text: A handy authority for regular training?

definitions.text: A handy authority for regular training?

parts.note: surface reading: some useful official body or expert to consult
setter's reading: a pass held in the hand that lets a commuter take the train every day

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a convenient expert to oversee a steady fitness programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like exercise, but it means travelling by train; 'handy' means carried in the hand, and the authority is permission to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-period travel pass permits repeated journeys, so for a daily rail commuter it is the carried permit that authorises the trip.

clue.text: See 1
Dismiss objection, showing old-fashioned brass

parts.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A boss fires someone over a complaint, revealing an outdated top brass.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is an early form of trombone, a Renaissance brass instrument, hence old-fashioned brass.

clue.text: European's caught by small deception

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: slight means small or slender
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European is tripped up by a minor trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition: E goes inside SLIGHT to make SLEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means cunning trickery or dexterous deceit, as in sleight of hand used by conjurors.

clue.text: Local branch hostile about new, detailed references

parts.note: a chapter is a local branch of a society or club

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word is wrapped around the short piece that follows

parts.note: adverse means hostile or unfavourable
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A local branch of some society is opposed to a new set of detailed citations.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma hides the join: 'about new' completes the wordplay, leaving 'detailed references' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from citing Bible passages exactly, so it means precise, authoritative sourcing for every point made.

clue.text: Cause a shock, turning crazy

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: to stun is to shock or stupefy

explanation.surface: Something shocking happens as someone goes mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal slang meaning mad or insane, an adjective just like crazy.

clue.text: Express needs someone to supply information for growth

parts.note: to couch something is to express it in particular words
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: An express train or newspaper needs an informant to keep growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a train or paper but is the verb, as in couching a request in polite terms; a grass in British slang is someone who informs to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Couch grass is a creeping weed that spreads through gardens, a type of plant growth that gardeners fight.

clue.text: Suffering after long ride, goes off, angry about it

indicators.note: about means around, and 'it' points back to the previous words, which are placed inside

parts.note: sore is informal for annoyed or angry
an egg that addles has gone off or turned rotten

explanation.surface: After a long journey something rots, and someone is cross about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Eggs that have gone off are said to be addled; 'it' in the clue points back to 'goes off' as the piece to be enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who spends hours on horseback or a bicycle ends up chafed and aching where they sit.

clue.text: Opportunity to back Othello, perhaps?

indicators.note: backing means moving in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: room means scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: Someone gets a chance to support a theatrical production of Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice, so he is an example of the North African people named here.

clue.text: Valuable support offered at end of appointment

definitions.text: Valuable support offered at end of appointment

parts.words: Valuable support offered at end of appointment
parts.note: surface reading: useful help given as a meeting or consultation finishes
setter's reading: the appointment is a job, and its end is when an employee leaves with a large payment

explanation.surface: Someone gets useful help just as a meeting is wrapping up.
explanation.walkthrough: An appointment can be a post as well as a meeting; the valuable support is a farewell payout, and a handshake is what you offer at parting.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a generous severance sum paid to a senior employee on retirement or dismissal, the money cushioning departure.

clue.text: Soldier in line about to make a mistake

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word encloses the word for blundering

parts.note: a tier is a row or line, as of seats
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A soldier standing in formation is about to slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: A Terrier is a member of Britain's part-time Territorial Army, so the soldier is not a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrier is British informal for a member of the Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve force of part-time soldiers.

clue.text: Plant affected by one working

parts.note: camp means affected or theatrically exaggerated
I is the Roman numeral for one; 'by' places it next to the previous piece
on means functioning or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A factory or a plant is affected by a single employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a flowering plant of the pink family, with red or white blooms found in hedgerows.

clue.text: Grant thinker new role, being chivalrous?

definitions.note: read as a noun: a chivalrous being

indicators.note: taking a new role means changing character, so these letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: the two words supply all twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A philosopher is offered a new part and acts gallantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being chivalrous' looks like an adjective phrase, but 'being' is a noun here: a creature who is chivalrous.
explanation.definitionFit: A wandering medieval horseman seeking adventures to prove his gallantry is the archetype of a chivalrous person.

clue.text: See 25
Held by a marvellous spell —

parts.note: surface reading: caught up in a wonderful period of time, the start of a chain of linked clues
setter's reading: the spell is a magic charm, and someone held by one is bewitched

explanation.walkthrough: This opens a chain of clues joined by dashes; 'spell' suggests a stretch of time but means a magical incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewitched or charmed means being under a magic spell, and also being delighted.

clue.text: 3 — but duck is broken suddenly, when scoring

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and reassembled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the zero-shaped letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman's duck ruins a sudden innings, continuing the dash-linked chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' looks like cricket after 'duck' but means writing a musical score; a duck in cricket is a batsman out for nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Subito is the Italian direction on sheet music meaning suddenly or immediately, so it is used when scoring music.

clue.text: No rise? Debts to be paid? It's familiar, unfortunately —

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill or rise, as on Dartmoor
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: No pay rise and bills to settle: a sadly familiar story.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hill, common in the moorlands of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being widely known for something bad, such as a scandal or crime, is fame of the unfortunate kind.

clue.text: 5 — Mike's stony broke!

indicators.note: something broke has been smashed, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer named Mike has lost all his money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stony broke' is British slang for penniless, but here the two words split into fodder and signal; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson is the American former world heavyweight boxing champion, so his surname is clued by his first name.

clue.text: Split accentuated by bust-up, perhaps —

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a division or splitting apart
second meaning: the hollow between the breasts, enhanced by a push-up bra

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust-up' looks like a quarrel causing the split, but read literally it is lifting the bust.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a division along a line, as in geology or politics, and the visible line between a woman's breasts.

clue.text: 7 — composer's given furious glare

indicators.note: furious suggests wild, violent agitation, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer is fixed with an angry stare, ending the dash-linked chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Instant sign of boredom? Time for a look at the future

parts.note: a second is an instant or moment
a sigh is a sign of weariness or boredom
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bored moment passes and it is time to consider what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the supposed psychic power of foreseeing events, a clairvoyant glimpse of what is to come.

clue.text: He may take responsibility if the Ashes are lost

definitions.text: He may take responsibility if the Ashes are lost

parts.words: He may take responsibility if the Ashes are lost
parts.note: surface reading: an England cricket captain or selector carrying the blame for losing the Ashes series
setter's reading: ash trees are dying, and an arborist is the one who tends them

explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia; here the ashes are ash trees whose care falls to a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who cuts, treats and removes diseased or dying trees would be called in when ash trees fail.

clue.text: Rich uncle (old, not posh) wasted an account

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined or squandered, so the remaining letters are scrambled
not means without, so the letter for posh is struck out of the collection

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
U means upper-class or posh, in the old British usage of U and non-U

explanation.surface: A wealthy uncle, elderly and unrefined, squandered the money in a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: Add O to RICH UNCLE, take out the U, then rearrange. 'Account' looks like banking but means a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical record of events in order of time, a narrative report of what happened.

clue.text: Love having a party — make allowances

parts.note: taken as written
a do is an informal party or celebration
to ration is to give out fixed allowances

explanation.surface: Romance blooms at a party where someone must be forgiving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make allowances' sounds like being tolerant, but it means doling out fixed shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and worship, a noun that can replace love in most sentences.

clue.text: Very short of ships in Grimsby, at first

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the port's name

explanation.surface: Grimsby, an English fishing port, is very short of ships at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Grimsby is a fishing port in north-east England, which makes the shortage of ships plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means lasting a very brief time, as in a fleeting glimpse, so it is short in duration.

clue.text: Type of nucleus is more unstable

indicators.note: something unstable will not keep its form, so these letters shift into a new order

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A physicist notes that one kind of atomic nucleus is less stable than another.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear isomer is an atomic nucleus in an excited energy state, one of several forms with the same composition.

clue.text: Film star has role that's different and new

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters appear in an altered order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An actor lands a fresh, unusual part in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is the Italian actress, an Oscar-winning screen icon, so she is a movie star.

clue.text: Is it right to interrupt this outrageous modern artist?

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so the letter goes inside the other word
outrageous suggests wild and shocking, so these letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether it is acceptable to heckle a shocking contemporary artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Damien Hirst is famous for pickled animals, which makes 'outrageous' an apt surface word.
explanation.definitionFit: Damien Hirst is a leading British contemporary artist, famous for shark in formaldehyde works.
